claims.text: If the airway is involved, securing it comes first.
claims.quote: For acute angioedema, first make sure the airway is secure;

claims.text: Unless the angioedema is clearly bradykinin-mediated (eg, ACE inhibitor, hereditary or acquired), give epinephrine IM or subcutaneously as for anaphylaxis.
claims.quote: Unless the mechanism is obviously bradykinin-mediated (eg, due to use of an ACE inhibitor or to known hereditary or acquired angioedema), epinephrine should be administered IM or subcutaneously as for anaphylaxis.

claims.text: Bradykinin-mediated swelling may take more than 30 minutes to subside,
claims.quote: However, in bradykinin-mediated angioedema, edema may take > 30 minutes to subside after treatment begins.
if the airway is affected, give epinephrine subcutaneously or IM unless the cause is obviously bradykinin-mediated angioedema, which is more likely to require endotracheal intubation.

claims.text: Oropharyngeal or airway angioedema: subcutaneous epinephrine 0.3 mL of 1:1000 solution and hospital admission; on discharge, supply and teach an epinephrine autoinjector
claims.quote: Patients who have angioedema involving the oropharynx or any involvement of the airway should receive subcutaneous epinephrine 0.3 mL of 1:1000 solution and be admitted to the hospital. On discharge, patients should be supplied with and trained in the use of an auto-injectable epinephrine pen.

claims.text: Severe mast cell–mediated reactions: always carry an autoinjector and oral antihistamines, self-treat quickly, then go to the emergency department
claims.quote: Patients who have severe mast cell–mediated reactions should be advised to always carry a prefilled, self-injecting syringe of epinephrine (ie, an autoinjector) and oral antihistamines and, if a severe reaction occurs, to self-administer these treatments as quickly as possible and then go to the emergency department.

claims.text: Not shown to be effective in bradykinin-mediated angioedema (nor are glucocorticoids or antihistamines)
claims.quote: For bradykinin-mediated angioedema, epinephrine, glucocorticoids, and antihistamines have not been shown to be effective.
